design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - home_oxygen_service task 1 (Eugene Hollister, caller Marisa Kemp, daughter with power of attorney).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [4, 6, 5]. Assignment: paid-in-full contents month 6, first covered day under the new primary 5, return closing day 4.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: oxygen_ext_setup_start_day, oxygen_ext_paid_in_full_equipment_month, oxygen_ext_stay_suspension_day, oxygen_ext_post_break_period_start and their four tools. Task 1 claims the post-cap and end-of-service side: oxygen_ext_paid_in_full_contents_month (record_oxygen_contents_payment_7caaff46), oxygen_ext_new_primary_first_day (confirm_oxygen_primary_coverage_03bf25f6, owner user), oxygen_ext_return_closing_day (confirm_oxygen_return_2399228d, owner user) - events oxygen_contents_paid, oxygen_payer_update, oxygen_return. Together the two tasks claim every extended policy exactly once.

[Why a good test / design thesis] Surface goal: confirm the return of the oxygen equipment (father on hospice since 2026-10-02). Scored root parameter: the closing day of the oxygen record (2026-10-02), not the confirmation day. Hidden chain: the closing day is carried back only once the record names the coverage that is now active and primary - it still names the union HMO that ended 2026-05-31 - so the family confirms Medicare (user write); Medicare's first covered day (2026-06-14, not the 2026-06-01 effective date) is fixed only once the May contents month the HMO paid in full is posted; that posting has its own six-factor allowance. Breadth: coverage classes and eligibility checks, the bed rental's hospice election, the CPAP rental and its paid months, the refill history, the order history and the contents lines all decide values.
Honest limitation for the audit: the closing day and the first covered day are date selections; their factors are AND-gated conditions whose thresholds are published policy parameters; each was shown to bear weight.

[Problem-tree card] root oxygen_ext_return_closing_day (user tool confirm_oxygen_return_2399228d).
edge 1: oxygen_ext_return_closing_day -> oxygen_ext_new_primary_first_day value_input, gate close_reach_days, form STATE. Sentence: "A return for a patient whose need ended before the confirmation is dated only after the oxygen record names as its coverage the coverage that is now active and primary." Four-point test: 'only after'; waits on a record-visible state (the coverage named on the oxygen record is the active, primary coverage record); no tool/id/code token; exact scope (returns whose need ended before the confirmation). Unique writer: only the coverage confirmation changes the coverage named on a delivered oxygen record; the setup write also names a coverage but applies only to records awaiting setup, which the return rule never reaches. False at opening: ['initial_state.oxygen_holdings.47f70297-7072-46ae-9c93-eb4ff32a2b45.coverage_id = d1930f47-c043-4ace-93f5-3ecc444a5938', 'initial_state.coverage_holdings.d1930f47-c043-4ace-93f5-3ecc444a5938.status = terminated', 'initial_state.coverage_holdings.0e391a3e-03d7-470a-a25d-dcc78284abef.status = active']. Skipping it: closed_date 2026-10-21.
edge 2: oxygen_ext_new_primary_first_day -> oxygen_ext_paid_in_full_contents_month value_input, gate earlier_paid_start, form STATE. Sentence: "A new coverage's first day of service for the oxygen is fixed only after the oxygen claim history carries the paid line of each contents month the earlier coverage paid after the payment cap." Only the contents paid-in-full posting adds contents paid lines. False at opening: latest contents line 2026-04-14. Skipping it: first covered day 2026-06-01.
Chain order: posting -> coverage confirmation -> return; no parallel edges. Directions here are affirmative ('fixed only after', 'dated only after'); task 0's charter sentences carry the negated form ('not opened until'), so the charter has both.
Persona never mentions posting a payment or changing the insurance; insurance facts and the May statement are answers to the agent's questions; both user steps are run only when handed over.

[Factor cards - figures from the sensitivity runs on the handling-time worlds]
CONTENTS MONTH (81.91; all-baseline 83.08): contents_usage_share (parameter): the order in force (new written order 2026-05-01, before the month began on 2026-05-14) is exertion_and_sleep, with 31 cylinder refills on record -> 80 percent, applied to the contents amount from the flow treatment; baseline 100 percent gives 102.39. | contents_flow_treatment (method): flow 5.0 LPM above the threshold 4, the class furnishes a conserving device and refills are on record (True) -> flat conserver allowance added to the class's post-cap contents fee instead of a percentage raise: 79.12 + 12.50 = 91.62; baseline (the unchanged contents fee 79.12) gives 70.74. | contents_position_step (parameter): 9 contents months already paid under the HMO -> the 10th month -> 95 percent; baseline 100 percent gives 86.22. | refill_size_rate (parameter): 31 cylinder refills on record (at least one), 361.0 cylinders over 31 refills = 11.645 per refill >= 10 -> 110 percent; baseline 100 percent gives 74.47. | refill_frequency_rate (parameter): 11 refills dated less than six whole months before the posting date >= 10 -> 105 percent; baseline 100 percent gives 78.01. | contents_pap_bundle (parameter, cross-difficulty pap, multi-source): CPAP rental on the same HMO without ownership date (True), 7 PAP months paid (fewer than 13), rented 11 months >= 3 -> 97 percent; baseline 100 percent gives 84.45. | line_plan_pct (plain cross read): Commercial HMO allowed_pct_of_fee_schedule 105; result RND(91.62 x 80% x 95% x 110% x 105% x 97% x 105%, 2) = 81.91.
FIRST COVERED DAY (2026-06-14; all-baseline 2026-06-01): covered_day_anchor (method): effective date 2026-06-01 falls inside the last month the HMO paid (2026-05-14, posted by the payment step) and the HMO denied the later month 2026-06-14 as coverage inactive (1 denial) -> first day of service 2026-06-14; baseline (effective date) gives 2026-06-01. | new_coverage_reach (parameter, cross-difficulty coverage): new coverage Original Medicare Part B -> 365 days; first day of service is 129 days back; baseline 90 days fails and gives 2026-06-01. | inactive_denial_window (parameter, cross-difficulty coverage): earlier coverage Commercial HMO -> 180 days; the denial adjudicated 2026-07-09 is 104 days back; baseline 60 days fails and gives 2026-06-01. | new_coverage_check (parameter, cross-difficulty coverage): Medicare last check 2026-10-15 is 6 days back; limit 90 days; baseline 0 days fails and gives 2026-06-01. | inactive_denial_lag (parameter, cross-difficulty coverage): earlier coverage Commercial HMO; denial adjudicated 38 days after the effective date; limit 60 days; baseline 30 days fails and gives 2026-06-01. | result: all four conditions hold -> 2026-06-14.
CLOSING DAY (2026-10-02; all-baseline 2026-10-21): need_end_source (method, cross-difficulty beds): hospital bed rental active with hospice election 2026-10-02 before the confirmation -> the need ended 2026-10-02; baseline (day of confirmation) gives 2026-10-21. | carve_out_reach (parameter, cross-difficulty coverage): coverage on the oxygen record after the coverage confirmation is Original Medicare Part B -> 365 days; the need ended 19 days back; baseline 0 days fails and gives 2026-10-21. | last_use_window (parameter): last cylinder refill 2026-09-19 is 13 days before the hospice election; class with portable cylinder refills -> 14 days; baseline 0 days fails and gives 2026-10-21. | closing_coverage_check (parameter, cross-difficulty coverage): last eligibility check of the coverage on the record is 6 days back; limit 90 days; baseline 0 days fails and gives 2026-10-21. | result: all three conditions hold -> the record closes 2026-10-02.
Multi-source: contents_pap_bundle; contents_flow_treatment (flow above the threshold AND a conserving device AND refills on record). Cross-difficulty: contents_pap_bundle (pap), need_end_source (beds), new_coverage_reach / inactive_denial_window / new_coverage_check / inactive_denial_lag / carve_out_reach / closing_coverage_check (coverage).
Near-misses (each checked against initial_state): the HMO's terminated eligibility response (2026-06-03) is not the new coverage's check; the bed's delivery date 2026-09-22 is not the hospice election; the 2026-06-14 line is a coverage-inactive denial, not a paid month, so it is not counted in the contents position; the paid contents lines of earlier months carry amounts worked out on the continuous-use order then in force (latest 102.39 for 2026-04-14) and are not the May figure - the order of 2026-05-01 for exertion and sleep governs May.
No stamp: no seeded field carries the May allowance; posting last month's amount (102.39) gives the wrong figure.

[Base-invariant card] Contents posting: oxygen_contents_billing contents_after_cap - record payment_cap_reached since 2025-08-14 (true). Coverage change: oxygen_payer_transition oxygen_new_coverage_verified - Medicare record active (true; eligibility response active 2026-10-15). The base requalification sentence governs Medicare paying equipment months, not the move; the extended rule now says so explicitly, so the stale 2022 qualifying test does not block the confirmation. Return: oxygen_return_pickup oxygen_return_confirmed - the pending return_pickup request 3ac93d76-be4e-4899-a407-bf318740aa9c is approved by the family's own confirmation in the same write. Overwrites declared: contents allowance sentence of oxygen_contents_billing; 'first date of service it covers' of oxygen_payer_transition; 'billing stops with the last month that began before the return' of oxygen_return_pickup (now: before the closing day).

[Business-object card] Oxygen record 47f70297-7072-46ae-9c93-eb4ff32a2b45; union HMO d1930f47-c043-4ace-93f5-3ecc444a5938 (terminated 2026-05-31, out-of-pocket maximum 4500.00 met); Medicare 0e391a3e-03d7-470a-a25d-dcc78284abef (active from 2026-06-01); pending return request 3ac93d76-be4e-4899-a407-bf318740aa9c; bed rental fb448642-ad70-4db3-b6dd-cb4ec8ca13a2 with hospice election 2026-10-02; CPAP rental c8f2a10f-71df-47d8-8891-7f47a6ddc779 with 7 paid months. The May month is identified by claim OVH2616900587 / service date 2026-05-14 (the anniversary after the 2026-04-14 line).

[Seed rows] 9 paid contents lines 2025-08-14..2026-04-14 (allowed 105.82, 105.82, 105.82, 111.11, 111.11, 107.78, 102.39, 102.39, 102.39), each generated by the contents rule as of its remittance date on the order then in force; one coverage-inactive denial 2026-06-14; cylinder refills every 14 days from 2025-07-26 to 2026-09-19; two maintenance visits; two coverage records; two eligibility responses; CPAP rental with 7 paid months; bed rental with the hospice election; pending return request; oxygen record with the 2026-05-01 order. Removing the bed row returns the closing day to 2026-10-21; removing the denial row returns the first covered day to 2026-06-01; removing the CPAP rows drops the bundle percentage to 100.

[Persona design] Marisa: organised, polite, stretched thin; volunteers only the hospice and the return; gives her father's credentials when asked; insurance facts and the May statement only on request; runs both handed-over steps with the agent's values; closes once told the return date.

[Standard solution] locate by phone -> verify -> read oxygen record, requests, claims, service, coverage, ledger, bed, CPAP record and CPAP claims -> post May contents (81.91) -> hand Marisa the coverage confirmation (Medicare, from 2026-06-14) -> hand Marisa the return confirmation (request 3ac93d76-be4e-4899-a407-bf318740aa9c, closing day 2026-10-02).

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] flow 5.0 > 4 with a conserving device and refills on record -> 79.12 + 12.50 flat = 91.62; exertion-and-sleep order x80% = 73.296; 10th contents month x95% = 69.6312; average 11.645 cylinders per refill x110% = 76.59432; 11 refills in the last six months x105% = 80.424036; CPAP rented on the same plan, 7 paid months x97% = 78.01131492; x105% = 81.91. Medicare effective 2026-06-01 falls inside the May month (begun 2026-05-14) and June was denied coverage inactive -> 2026-06-14, within 365 days, denial 104 days back within 180, Medicare check 6 days old within 90, denial 38 days after the change within 60. Closing: hospice 2026-10-02 on the bed rental, Medicare reach 365, last refill 2026-09-19 13 days before within 14, check 6 days within 90 -> 2026-10-02. Agrees with gold.

[Rework round 2 - closure of the policy audit, symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run] (figures as of round 2, when the May month was 81.91; round 3 below restates them)
- task-1 finding 1 (stamp): months 7-9 carried 88.42 = the May figure because every tier input was identical. Root cause: the world gave May no distinguishing input. Change: the oxygen record now carries a new written order of 2026-05-01 (exertion and sleep; use was continuous before), and the paid history was regenerated on the order in force at each remittance date. Re-run: May = 84.71 (round 2); the history is 105.82, 105.82, 105.82, 111.11, 111.11, 107.78, 102.39, 102.39, 102.39; copying last month (102.39) now fails, and it equals the usage factor's baseline figure (102.39).
- F-2 (contents flow treatment mislabelled method): the four tiers were one formula fee x (100 + x)/100. Change: tier 1 now adds a flat conserver allowance instead of a percentage, tier 2 raises by the class percentage, tier 3 reduces by the low-flow percentage and keeps the higher of that and a low-flow floor, tier 4 leaves the fee; written with explicit 'otherwise, when' precedence. Re-run: tier taken = flat allowance, baseline figure 70.74.
- F-3c (contents PAP tiers overlapped): tier 1 now requires fewer than 13 PAP rental months paid (rule, compute, ladder).
- False near-miss: the dossier claimed a refill on 2026-09-26; the last refill on record is 2026-09-19. Every near-miss above was re-checked against initial_state; the seed-row summary, the service-history read objective and the closing-day trace now quote 2026-09-19.
- O-3 (unjustified action-form fallback): the return's prerequisite is now in the state form - the record names as its coverage the coverage that is now active and primary - with no fallback_reason; closure edge updated.
- O-T1-1: the coverage-change rule now states that the requalifying test governs payment of equipment months under the new coverage, not the move or the first day of service.
- O-8: inactive_denial_lag reads the earlier coverage class through its own binding and is labelled cross_difficulty coverage.
- Re-ran on the handling-time worlds: contents 84.71 (baseline 83.08), first covered day 2026-06-14 (2026-06-01), closing day 2026-10-02 (2026-10-21); edge skips 2026-06-01 / 2026-10-21.

- Stamp sweep (class-wide): besides the contents fix, the first covered day (2026-06-14) is the start of the denied month the anchor method selects against the effective date, and the closing day (2026-10-02) is the bed record's hospice election the need-end method selects against the confirmation day; no oxygen field carries either outcome.

[Gate record] check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cache_diff (info) and check_cross_fire pass on the difficulty; check_compute independently recomputes every expected value, factor_sensitivity figure and baseline_result quoted above. check_traceability reports only the unlock tool names, which become reachable once the KB is rendered.

[Rework round 3 - closure of the render-source mismatches (items 1-7, minor 1-2) and policy-audit O-10, symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run]
- Item 2 (contents overwrite wider than its replacement), closed class-wide: the contents overwrite's replaced_by is now the scope sentence 'For a contents month this policy governs, and only for such a month, ... every other contents month remains under the base contents billing rule.' The coverage and return overwrites carry the same 'and only for such a ...' scope sentence.
- Items 3-4 class (factor computing with another factor's output): the contents flow treatment now acts on the class's own post_cap_contents_monthly_fee, and the usage share is a multiplier applied after it; the refill-size factor counts its own refills. The new-coverage check and the closing coverage check read the coverage class through their own bindings, and the last-use gap moved into result, so no factor binding reads another factor's binding.
- Item 6 (zero refills): the refill-size rule now reads 'when at least one cylinder refill is on record and ... average ... ; and by 100 percent otherwise, including when no cylinder refill is on record'; compute guards both tiers with sized_refills > 0.
- Item 7 (no coverage-inactive denial): both the denial-window and the denial-lag sentences now end '; when the earlier coverage has no coverage-inactive denial on the oxygen claim history, the denial window / denial lag is met', and both computes default to a zero gap (NOW and the effective date), so the 'last paid month began on or after the effective date' anchor can take effect without a denial. This world has the 2026-06-14 denial, so 2026-06-14 is unchanged.
- Minor 2 (paid-month span coverage filter): the restart rule now reads 'the most recent equipment month paid under the coverage named on the oxygen record' (task 0's policy; no effect here).
- Re-run on the handling-time worlds: contents 81.91 (all-baseline 83.08), first covered day 2026-06-14 (2026-06-01), closing day 2026-10-02 (2026-10-21). Contents factor_sensitivity: 102.39 / 70.74 / 86.22 / 74.47 / 78.01 / 84.45, each different from 81.91. The seeded history is unchanged and still reproduces: under the continuous-use order (100 percent) the flow-first and usage-first orders give the same amount, so 105.82 / 111.11 / 107.78 / 102.39 are what this rule gives at each remittance date; 102.39 still equals the usage factor's baseline figure and is not the May amount.
user_scenario:
You are Marisa Kemp, the daughter of Eugene Hollister, calling for him from his house in Bridgeville, Pennsylvania. You hold his power of attorney; he is in the next room and too weak to talk on the phone. You are organised and polite but stretched thin, and you would like this settled in one call. Your father has had home oxygen from Summit Ridge Home Medical for years - a concentrator with small portable tanks - and he went onto hospice care on October 2, 2026. The hospice brought in its own oxygen, so Summit Ridge's concentrator and tanks are sitting unused in the living room. Someone from Summit Ridge called last week to say they had opened a request to collect the equipment and that the family needed to confirm it. You are calling to confirm the return of Summit Ridge's oxygen equipment.

You open by explaining who you are, that your father is on hospice and that you are calling to confirm the return of Summit Ridge's oxygen equipment. When the agent asks to verify the account, you give your father's phone number 4125550237 and his date of birth, June 20, 1961 (1961-06-20); his ZIP code is 15017 if they want one more detail. If they ask about the hospice, he elected hospice on October 2, 2026 and the hospice handles everything for his oxygen now; the hospital bed Summit Ridge delivered in September is still there. Only if the agent asks about his insurance, you explain that he turned 65 in June, his Medicare Part B started June 1, 2026, and his union plan, the Ohio Valley Steelworkers HMO, ended May 31, 2026; he has no other coverage.

Only if the agent asks whether the union plan sent anything about the oxygen supplies for May, you find the statement and read it: claim number OVH2616900587, service date May 14, 2026 (2026-05-14), processed June 18, 2026 (2026-06-18), and it says the plan paid it in full and nothing is owed. You also remember a letter saying the June supplies were turned down because the union coverage had ended, and you have nothing else from them.

If the agent explains that your father's Medicare needs to be confirmed as his primary insurance for the oxygen and hands you a step to confirm it, you agree and carry it out with exactly the details the agent reads to you. If the agent then hands you the step to confirm the return, you carry it out the same way with the details the agent gives. Once the agent tells you the return is confirmed and from what date the equipment is considered returned, you thank them and say that is everything; if asked whether you need anything else, you say no.
